newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firms on EU rebate, weaker currency.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firms on EU rebate, weaker currency.

text.p: French wheat prices were firmer on Friday after the European Union raised the rebate applying to soft wheat exports at its weekly grain auction on Thursday.
Support also came from a weaker currency, which is making French wheat more competitive, and from fears that a truck strike now in its fifth day may disrupt grain transport, they said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 860 francs for December delivery and at 840 francs for January-March delivery, both up five on Thursday.
The franc has weakened after a call by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for franc depreciation reopened the debate on the merits of European economic and monetary union.
On Thursday the European Union raised the refund on soft wheat exports to 16.59 Ecus per tonne from 15.97 Ecus last week, appearing to let the EU undercut U.S. prices for the first time in months.
But one EU grain official said the EU had not changed its wheat export policy and was still pricing its wheat against U.S. wheat.
Wheat futures volume on MATIF was a fairly strong 262 lots at 1523 GMT, with the February 97 expiry quoted at 874 francs, down four francs on Thursday.
